blocks.text: Have you ever lent money to a friend and wondered if you'd ever get it back? In business, this situation is managed through bad and doubtful debts.

blocks.markdown: In accounting, businesses often sell goods on credit. However, not all customers will pay their debts. To handle this, accountants use the concepts of bad debts and doubtful debts.

blocks.title: Bad Debt
blocks.text: A bad debt is an amount owed to a business that is considered irrecoverable and is written off as an expense.

blocks.markdown: When a debt is confirmed to be uncollectible, it is written off as a bad debt. This reduces the accounts receivable and increases expenses. On the other hand, a provision for doubtful debts is an estimate of the debts that might become uncollectible in the future.

blocks.title: Provision for Doubtful Debts
blocks.text: This is an estimation of the amount of debts that may not be collected in the future, creating a reserve to cover potential losses.

blocks.title: Recording a Bad Debt
blocks.prompt: Let's say a customer, Chinedu, owes your business ₦50,000, but you have confirmed he cannot pay. How do you record this?

steps.text: 1. Identify the amount to be written off as a bad debt.
2. Debit the Bad Debt Expense account with ₦50,000.
3. Credit the Accounts Receivable account with ₦50,000.

blocks.answer: The journal entry will be: Debit Bad Debt Expense ₦50,000; Credit Accounts Receivable ₦50,000.

blocks.markdown: Adjusting the provision for doubtful debts involves estimating the future uncollectible debts. If the provision needs to increase, an expense is recorded. Conversely, if it decreases, an income is recorded.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always distinguish between bad debts (actual losses) and doubtful debts (estimated potential losses) in your answers.

points: Bad debts are written off when confirmed irrecoverable.
Provisions for doubtful debts are estimates for potential future losses.
